widget.instructions: Press Play to run the motion; scrub the time slider to inspect any instant.

stem: A car covers the first half of a trip at {{v1}} m/s and the second half (the same distance) at {{v2}} m/s.
What is its average speed for the whole trip?

hints.text: Pick a trip length, say 2d. How long does each half take?
Average speed = total distance ÷ total time.
Time for each half is d ÷ v; add them before dividing.

arithmetic-mean-speed.text: Averaging the two speeds treats the halves as equal times. The car spends longer on the slower half, so the average is lower.

dimension-mismatch.text: Check the unit: the answer is a velocity.

generic.text: Total distance ÷ total time; work out the time for each half.

workedSolution.text: Let each half be d. Times: d/{{v1}} and d/{{v2}}.
Average = 2d ÷ (d/{{v1}} + d/{{v2}}) = 2 × {{v1}} × {{v2}} ÷ ({{v1}} + {{v2}}) = {{ans}} m/s, less than the mean {{mean}} m/s.

args.text: More time is spent at the slower speed.

arithmetic-mean-speed.front: Half the distance at v₁, half at v₂: average speed?
arithmetic-mean-speed.back: 2v₁v₂ ÷ (v₁ + v₂), not (v₁ + v₂) ÷ 2: more time is spent at the slower speed.

accessibility.altText: Two lanes showing the car's speeds on the two halves.
